category: Control Panel, editors, panels and configuration
description: The EAGLE 9.6 working environment: the Control Panel with its tree view, menus and context menus, the Options dialogs (Directories, Backup/Locking, User interface, Set, Proxy), keyboard and mouse conventions, the board, schematic, library and text editor windows with their dockable panels (Inspector, Selection Filter, Sheets, Design Manager), forward & back annotation between schematic and board, command syntax, and the eagle/eaglecon command-line options.

tools.name: Control Panel
tools.description: The top-level EAGLE window. A tree view on the left groups files by type (Libraries, Design Blocks, Design Rules, User Language Programs, Scripts, CAM Jobs, Projects), each branch pointing to one or more directories from Options > Directories, and an information pane on the right shows the selected item's description plus a preview for devices, footprints, symbols and 3D packages. Descriptions come from the first non-blank line of a DESCRIPTION file (folders), the library/device/footprint/symbol/design-rules description, a ULP's #usage text, a script's leading comment or a CAM job's description.
tools.usage: Starts with eagle.exe; from any editor bring it to the front with Alt+0 or Window > Control Panel
tools.example: Expand Libraries > a library > click a device to see its package variants and preview; right-click a folder under Projects > New Project to create a project folder with its eagle.epf.
tools.notes: The status line shows the full path of the selected item. Since 9.1 the files installed with EAGLE are read-only and appear in 'examples' folders. After Autodesk's licensing shutdown (7 June 2026) the GUI stops at the Autodesk sign-in window; the command-line CAM Processor (eaglecon -X) still works without it.

tools.name: Control Panel pulldown menu
tools.description: The Control Panel menu bar. File holds New, Open, Open recent projects, Save all (also writes eagle.epf even if automatic project saving is off), Close project and Exit; View holds Refresh, Search in tree and Sort; Options opens the Directories, Backup, User interface, Data collection and use (anonymous analytics / e-mail communication) and Proxy settings dialogs. Window lists the Control Panel and every numbered editor window, and Help offers General, Context, Control Panel, Check for Update (configurable automatic check, optionally including betas) and About EAGLE.
tools.usage: Control Panel > File | View | Options | Window | Help

parameters.name: File > New
parameters.description: New board, schematic, design block, library, CAM job, ULP, script, text file or project.

parameters.name: Window
parameters.description: Alt+0 raises the Control Panel, Alt+<n> the editor window numbered n (Windows and Linux).

parameters.name: Help > Check for Update
parameters.description: Queries for a newer EAGLE version; Configure sets how often this happens at start-up (default once a day).

tools.example: Options > Directories... to add D:\Company\lbr to the Libraries path; Window > 2 Board - demo2.brd (or Alt+2) to switch to that editor.
tools.notes: Exit stores the window state so the next start restores it; Alt+X leaves EAGLE from any window while the pulldown menu is enabled.

tools.name: Control Panel context menu
tools.description: Right-clicking a tree item offers the actions valid for it: New Folder, Edit Description, Rename, Copy, Delete, Use / Use all / Use none (which libraries ADD searches), Update and Update in Library (refresh parts from this library), Add to Schematic / Add to Board, Copy to Library, New package variant in Library, Open/Close Project, New, Open, Print..., Run in ... (ULP), Execute in ... (script) and Load into Board (design rules). Most actions also work by drag and drop: a device dropped on a schematic starts ADD, a ULP or script dropped on an editor runs, a .dru dropped on a board editor is applied and a drawing dropped on its editor is loaded.
tools.usage: Right-click an item in the Control Panel tree (or drag it onto an editor window)
tools.example: With a board open: right-click design rules > examples > Eurocircuits > eC_Defaults > eC_2Layer_PClass6_BaseCopperO18_eCDefault.dru > Load into Board.
tools.notes: Print... from the context menu prints the file as stored on disk, not unsaved editor changes, and draws board polygons only as outlines; open the board, run RATSNEST and use PRINT to print calculated polygons.

tools.name: Search in tree
tools.description: Searches names and descriptions of all Control Panel tree items, including devices and footprints inside libraries. Several blank-separated words must all match (case-insensitive); '*' matches any run of non-blank characters, '?' exactly one, and a literal wildcard is escaped as '\*'. Starting the search from a branch's context menu limits it to that branch.
tools.usage: Control Panel > View > Search in tree, then type the pattern in the search bar
tools.example:
74* nand     (finds NAND devices of the 74xx series)
40\*14      (searches for the literal text 40*14)

tools.name: Projects and eagle.epf
tools.description: A project is a folder in the Projects path that contains an eagle.epf file and usually the schematic, board, private libraries, scripts and manufacturing output. Opening a project (click its gray marker, double-click it or use File > Open recent projects) restores the open editor windows, the libraries in use and the CHANGE and menu presets stored in eagle.epf; closing it writes these settings back when 'Automatically save project file' is enabled.
tools.usage: Control Panel > Projects > right-click a folder > New Project; open/close with the marker next to the project name
tools.example: eagle D:\Work\PowerSupply\eagle.epf     (start EAGLE with this project loaded)
tools.notes: A file named eagle.epf given on the command line is loaded as a project file. EAGLE asks before overwriting an eagle.epf written by another version; ULPs see the current one as eagle_epf.

tools.name: Options > Directories
tools.description: Defines the search path of each file type shown in the Control Panel (libraries, design rules, User Language programs, scripts, CAM jobs, projects, plus documentation and user SPICE model folders). An entry may list several directories separated by ';' on Windows (':' on Linux/macOS); OPEN, USE, SCRIPT and RUN search them left to right, and a folder reached through a file dialog is appended implicitly. The variables $HOME and $EAGLEDIR can be used, and 'Include EAGLE examples' shows or hides the read-only example folders.
tools.usage: Control Panel > Options > Directories...

parameters.name: $HOME
parameters.description: On Windows the EAGLE_HOME environment variable if set, otherwise the 'My Documents' folder from the registry; user files go to $HOME\EAGLE by default.

parameters.name: $EAGLEDIR
parameters.description: The EAGLE installation directory.

parameters.name: Include EAGLE examples
parameters.description: Toggles visibility of the example directories (libraries, CAM jobs, design rules, ULPs, scripts, projects).

tools.example:
Libraries: $HOME\EAGLE\libraries;D:\Company\lbr
Design rules: D:\Company\dru;$HOME\EAGLE\design rules
CAM jobs: D:\Company\cam
tools.notes: New boards read default.dru from the first directory of the Design rules path. The paths are stored in eaglerc and are available to ULPs as path_lbr[], path_dru[], path_ulp[], path_scr[], path_cam[] and path_epf[].

tools.name: Options > Backup / Locking
tools.description: Controls the backup and locking behaviour: how many numbered backups WRITE keeps (maximum backup level, default 9), the interval after which a modified drawing gets a safety copy (auto backup interval, default 5 minutes), whether the project file is saved automatically when a project is closed or EAGLE exits, and whether file locking is enabled. If you untick automatic project saving while a project is open, use File > Save all afterwards, otherwise the change is not stored in that project's eagle.epf.
tools.usage: Control Panel > Options > Backup...

parameters.name: Maximum backup level
parameters.description: Number of .x#1...x#9 backups kept per file (default 9).

parameters.name: Auto backup interval (minutes)
parameters.description: Maximum time before a safety copy .x## of a modified drawing is written (default 5).

parameters.name: Automatically save project file
parameters.description: Save open windows and settings to eagle.epf on close/exit.

parameters.name: Enable file locking
parameters.description: Create .<file>.lck lock files (same as SET LOCKING ON).

tools.example: Maximum backup level 3, Auto backup interval 2, Automatically save project file on, Enable file locking on.

tools.name: Automatic backup
tools.description: Each WRITE turns the previous version into a numbered backup with the extension pattern .x#n, where x is b (board), s (schematic), l (library) or d (design block) and n runs 1..9 with 1 the newest. Independently, a modified drawing is saved as a safety copy .x## after at most the auto backup interval; that copy is deleted after the next successful WRITE and can be renamed to .brd/.sch/.lbr/.dbl to recover work after a crash.
tools.usage: Automatic on WRITE and on the auto backup timer; configure in Options > Backup
tools.example:
copy board.b## board_recovered.brd     (recover the safety copy after a power failure)
del *.?#?                             (delete all numbered and safety backups in a folder)
tools.notes: Backups with the same number are not guaranteed to form a consistent board/schematic pair.

tools.name: File locking
tools.description: A file open in a drawing editor or the text editor is locked with a lock file named .<file>.lck beside it, released when the editor closes or loads another file. Opening a locked file offers to save under a different name, retry, delete the lock or ignore it (then the file must be saved under another name). With locking switched off EAGLE still respects other users' locks but creates none; the CAM Processor and read-only files are never locked.
tools.usage: SET LOCKING OFF | ON;   or Control Panel > Options > Backup/Locking
tools.example: SET LOCKING ON;     # e.g. demo2.brd is then locked by .demo2.brd.lck while open
tools.notes: Use the delete option to remove a stale lock left by a crash, and tell the lock owner if you delete an active lock. The setting is stored in eaglerc (the help says files are locked by default, the manual calls the checkbox off by default - check it after installation).

tools.name: Options > User interface
tools.description: Customises the look of the layout, schematic and library editors. Controls switches the pulldown menu, action toolbar, parameter toolbar, command buttons, textual command menu and sheet thumbnails on or off; Layout and Schematic choose a black, white or colored background and a small or large cursor; further options cover group annotations, the reading direction of vertical text, bubble help, user guidance, 'Always vector font', the mouse-wheel zoom factor and an external text editor.
tools.usage: Control Panel or any editor > Options > User interface...

parameters.name: Enable High DPI Scaling / Auto Screen Scale Factor
parameters.description: Set the Qt high-DPI attributes (Qt::AA_EnableHighDpiScaling, QT_AUTO_SCREEN_SCALE_FACTOR).

parameters.name: Vertical text
parameters.description: Reading direction (up/down) for new drawings and for the current drawing.

parameters.name: Always vector font
parameters.description: Display all texts in the built-in vector font; from an editor the sub-option 'Persistent in this drawing' stores this in the file.

parameters.name: Mouse wheel zoom
parameters.description: Zoom factor per wheel step; 0 disables wheel zoom, a negative value reverses the direction.

parameters.name: External text editor
parameters.description: Command line of an external editor (placeholders %F, %L, %C) or '-' to never open a text editor.

tools.example: Layout: Background black, Cursor large; Schematic: Background white; Misc: Always vector font on; Mouse wheel zoom 0 (wheel scrolls instead of zooming).
tools.notes: Using the vector font guarantees that texts look the same on screen, in PRINT output and in CAM data; with all Controls off only the command line remains.

tools.name: Options > Proxy settings
tools.description: Chooses how EAGLE's network functions connect: use the system proxy settings (default), no proxy, an HTTP proxy or a SOCKS5 proxy, with server, port and optional authentication. The Test settings button tries a connection with a 30-second timeout and shows a countdown and the result next to the button.
tools.usage: Control Panel > Options > Proxy settings...

parameters.name: Proxy type
parameters.description: Use system settings | No proxy | HTTP | SOCKS5.

parameters.name: Server / Port
parameters.description: Host name and port of the proxy.

parameters.name: Proxy server requires password
parameters.description: Enables user name and password fields for proxy authentication.

tools.example: Proxy type: HTTP, Server: proxy.company.local, Port: 8080 > Test settings.

tools.name: Modifier keys (Alt, Ctrl, Shift, Esc, cursor keys)
tools.description: Holding Alt switches to the alternate grid for fine positioning while the key is down. Ctrl + right click toggles to the corresponding wire bend style, Ctrl + left click triggers command-specific extras (for example MOVE grabbing an object at its origin) and Ctrl + right click selects a group; Shift + right click cycles bend styles backwards and Shift + left click applies commands to a higher-level object (for example DELETE). Esc cancels the current step of a command (clearing the command line first), and Cursor Up/Down browse the command-line history.
tools.usage: Hold Alt while moving | Ctrl/Shift + mouse click | Esc | Up/Down in the command line (use Cmd instead of Ctrl on macOS)
tools.example:
GRID MM 1 ALT MM 0.1;
MOVE     # then Ctrl+left-click a part to pick it at its origin, hold Alt to place it on the 0.1 mm grid
tools.notes: Some operating systems or window managers swallow certain modifier+mouse combinations, so a few of these functions may be unavailable.

tools.name: Mouse buttons and wheel
tools.description: The left button selects, draws and places. The center button changes the active layer in drawing commands (ARC, CIRCLE, LABEL, LINE, POLYGON, RECT, ROUTE, ROUTEDIFF, ROUTEMULTI, SMD, TEXT) or mirrors the attached object (ADD, COPY, INVOKE, MOVE, PASTE), and dragging with it pans the view. The right button rotates the attached object, changes the wire bend, selects a group or closes a polygon depending on the command, and on an object opens a context menu; the wheel zooms.
tools.usage: Left = select/place, Center = layer/mirror (drag = pan), Right = rotate/bend/group/context menu, Wheel = zoom
tools.example: ROUTE: click an airwire, press the center button to pick the next layer from the popup, right-click to cycle the bend style, left-click to place the vertex.

tools.name: Default function-key assignments
tools.description: EAGLE presets a few function keys for help and view control: F1 HELP, Alt+F2 WINDOW FIT, F2 WINDOW; (redraw), F3 WINDOW 2 (zoom in), F4 WINDOW 0.5 (zoom out), F5 WINDOW (@); (centre on the cursor) and F6 GRID; (grid on/off). Any function key F1..F12, letter or digit key (with Alt, Ctrl or Cmd) and Backspace can be reassigned with ASSIGN; the current table is shown in the Options > Assign dialog.
tools.usage: ASSIGN   (dialog)   |   ASSIGN key 'command sequence';
tools.example:
ASSIGN F7 'change layer top; route';
ASSIGN C+F10;     # remove an assignment
tools.notes: F1 opens the help page of the active command; outside the editors it opens context-sensitive help. HELP MOVE shows the page of a named command.

tools.name: default-assign.scr
tools.description: The shipped eagle.scr runs SCRIPT default-assign.scr, which defines the Ctrl/Alt shortcuts of EAGLE 9: in all editors Ctrl+M MOVE, Ctrl+Z UNDO, Ctrl+Y REDO, Ctrl+Shift+C COPY, Ctrl+Shift+A ADD, Ctrl+D DELETE, Ctrl+W WIRE, Ctrl+I INFO, Ctrl+T TEXT, Ctrl+Shift+N NAME, Ctrl+Shift+P POLYGON, Ctrl+F find.ulp, Ctrl+G NEWGROUP and Ctrl+Shift+G UNGROUP. Editor-specific sections (BRD:, SCH:, LBR:, DEV:, SYM:, PAC:) add routing, check and library shortcuts; edit a copy of the script to change them.
tools.usage: SCRIPT default-assign.scr;   (called automatically from eagle.scr)

parameters.name: BRD:
parameters.description: Ctrl+E ERRORS, Ctrl+Shift+D 'DRC;' (check without dialog), Ctrl+Shift+V VALUE, Ctrl+Shift+R RIPUP, Ctrl+H HOLE, Alt+G/P/W obstacle mode Ignore/Push/Walkaround, Alt+1..4 via patterns, Alt+A/S/D multi-route spacing, Alt+Q SWAPEND, Ctrl+1..7 ROUTE, ROUTEMULTI, ROUTEDIFF, QROUTEAIRWIRE, QROUTESIGNAL, QROUTEMULTI, QROUTESMOOTH.

parameters.name: SCH:
parameters.description: Ctrl+E ERRORS, Ctrl+Shift+E ERC, Ctrl+Shift+I INVOKE, Ctrl+Shift+V VALUE, Ctrl+Shift+S SMASH, Alt+N NET.

parameters.name: LBR: / DEV: / SYM: / PAC:
parameters.description: Ctrl+E EDIT; Alt+C CONNECT, Alt+P PACKAGE (device); Alt+P PIN (symbol); Ctrl+H HOLE, Alt+P PAD, Alt+S SMD (footprint).

tools.example:
BRD:
ASSIGN CS+D 'DRC;';     # run the DRC immediately
#ASSIGN CS+D DRC;       # alternative: open the Design Rules dialog
tools.notes: Default shortcuts were moved from eagle.scr into default-assign.scr so that updating eagle.scr does not overwrite personal assignments.

tools.name: Selecting objects in dense areas
tools.description: When several objects lie within the selection radius, EAGLE highlights one and asks 'Select highlighted object? (left=yes, right=next, ESC=cancel)'. Right click cycles to the next candidate, left click accepts and Esc aborts; if the first click was a right click, a context menu for the first object appears with 'Next' as its first entry. The radius is set with SET SELECT_FACTOR.
tools.usage: SET SELECT_FACTOR value;   (values < 1 are a factor, >= 1 a percentage of the visible drawing height/width)
tools.example: SET SELECT_FACTOR 0.01;     # 1 % selection radius for very dense boards
tools.notes: The Selection Filter panel reduces ambiguity further by limiting selectable object types and layers.

tools.name: Group default on
tools.description: An Options > Set > Misc checkbox that makes selection the default action when no command is active. With it on, a click-drag on any selected object moves the whole group, Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) adds or removes objects incrementally, left clicks starting off an object define a polygon selection, Esc clears the group and Backspace (Delete on Mac) deletes the selected objects.
tools.usage: Options > Set > Misc > Group default on
tools.example: Enable Group default on, drag a window around four resistors, Ctrl-click a fifth, then drag one of them to move all five; press Esc to clear the selection.

tools.name: Options > Set
tools.description: The settings dialog opened by SET without parameters. The Misc tab collects checkboxes and values such as Beep, Check connects, Undo, Optimizing, Ratsnest processes polygons, Display pad names, signal names on pads/traces, via lengths and drills, Auto end net and bus, Auto set junction, Auto set route width and drill, Group default on, minimum visible text and grid size, catch and select factor, snap length and the cross-reference label/part formats. The Colors tab edits the three 64-entry ARGB palettes (black, white, colored background), and the Drill tab maps hole diameters to drill-plan symbols (its Set button collects all diameters of the board).
tools.usage: Editor > Options > Set...   or type   SET
tools.notes: Settings are stored in the eaglerc user file. Live DRC is switched with a checkbox in the Set dialog or SET LIVE_DRC ON | OFF.

tools.name: Configuring EAGLE
tools.description: Besides the Control Panel dialogs, EAGLE is configured with editor commands typed in the command line or placed in eagle.scr. MENU and ASSIGN customise the text menu and keys; SET controls snapping (SNAP_LENGTH, CATCH_FACTOR, SELECT_FACTOR), menu contents (USED_LAYERS, WIDTH_MENU, DRILL_MENU, SMD_MENU, ...), wire bend, colors and fill per layer, display modes, mode switches (AUTO_JUNCTION, LIVE_DRC, OPTIMIZING, UNDO_LOG, CHECK_CONNECTS), panel visibility, move, obstacle and ripup modes and via patterns; CHANGE sets the defaults used for new objects (width, drill, diameter, shape, SMD size, text size, ratio, font, alignment and polygon parameters).
tools.usage: SET option value;   MENU ...;   ASSIGN ...;   CHANGE parameter value;   (interactively or in eagle.scr)

parameters.name: SET MOVE_MODE
parameters.description: PRESERVE_ANGLES | FREE | DISCONNECT.

parameters.name: SET OBSTACLE_MODE / LOOP_REMOVAL / VIA_PATTERN
parameters.description: Routing behaviour: IGNORE | WALKAROUND | PUSH; loop removal on/off; PERPENDICULAR | ANGLE_RIGHT | ANGLE_LEFT | STAGGER.

parameters.name: SET Ripup_mode
parameters.description: DEFAULT | SIGNAL | CONNECTED | CONNECTED_SAME_LAYER | ELEMENT_ELEMENT | ALL | ALL_POLYGONS.

parameters.name: SET DESIGN_MANAGER / INSPECTOR / SELECTION_FILTER / SHEETS / SINGLE_LAYER_MODE
parameters.description: OFF | ON | TOGGLE for the panels and single-layer display.

parameters.name: SET CONFIRM
parameters.description: YES | NO | OPT1..OPT9 | OFF: answer message dialogs automatically in scripts (use only around single commands).

tools.notes: Each *_MENU list holds at most 16 values; 'SET WIDTH_MENU;' restores the defaults.

tools.name: eagle.scr
tools.description: The start-up script that runs whenever a drawing is loaded into an editor (and when the drawing type changes in the library editor), taken from the project directory or the Scripts path. Labels SCH:, BRD:, LBR:, DEV:, SYM: and PAC: select the section executed for each editor. The shipped file calls default-assign.scr, adds MENU buttons (Search and order, PCB Service, PADS package import) and defines the board DISPLAY presets Preset_Top, Preset_Bottom and Preset_Standard.
tools.usage: Place eagle.scr in the Scripts path or the project folder; it runs automatically
tools.notes: Not executed when EAGLE is started with -C; -S names a different start-up script. Preset layer groups can only be edited in eagle.scr.

tools.name: eaglerc parameters (SET Parameter.Name)
tools.description: SET looks up any keyword it does not know among the eaglerc parameters, so fine-tuning switches that have no dialog can be changed with SET name value (the name is case-sensitive and must be written in full). Typical values are 0/1 to turn a behaviour off or on; screen-related changes may need a WINDOW; refresh.
tools.usage: SET Parameter.Name value;

parameters.name: Cmd.Copy.ClassicEagleMode
parameters.description: 1 = old COPY/CUT behaviour (takes effect in newly opened editors).

parameters.name: Cmd.Name.RenameEntireNetByDefault / Cmd.Name.RenameEntireSignalByDefault
parameters.description: Make NAME rename whole nets (and busses) or whole signals by default.

parameters.name: Erc.AllowUserOverrideConsistencyCheck
parameters.description: 1 = allow forcing annotation on slightly inconsistent files, at your own risk.

parameters.name: Interface.PreferredUnit
parameters.description: 0 automatic, 1 imperial, 2 metric units in dialog fields.

parameters.name: Interface.UseCtrlForPanning
parameters.description: 1 = pan with Ctrl + mouse movement as in old versions.

parameters.name: Option.LayerSequence
parameters.description: Rendering order of layers for printing/PDF, e.g. '123b * 123t'.

parameters.name: Option.RatsnestLimit, Option.ShowPartOrigins, Option.ShowTextOrigins, Option.ViaLength, Option.SignalNamesOnPads, Option.SignalNamesOnTraces
parameters.description: Ratsnest memory limit and display switches.

parameters.name: Sch.Cmd.Add.AlwaysUseDeviceNameAsValue, Warning.Cam.DrillsAndHolesConcurrent, Warning.PartHasNoUserDefinableValue
parameters.description: Value default and warning suppression switches.

tools.name: Board Editor
tools.description: The editor window for boards (*.brd). If a schematic with the same name exists in the same folder it is opened as well (minimised), because board edits that affect connectivity must be back-annotated to it. A single closed, non-self-intersecting outline on the Dimension layer is recognised as the board shape and drawn in a distinct colour; inner closed shapes and closed shapes on the Milling layer are treated as cutouts.
tools.usage: Control Panel > File > Open > Board, double-click a .brd, or EDIT name.brd
tools.notes: Like all editors it has a pulldown menu, action toolbar, parameter toolbar (changes with the active command), command toolbar, coordinate display, command line and status line.

tools.name: Schematic Editor
tools.description: The editor window for schematics (*.sch). If a board with the same name exists in the same folder it is opened as well (minimised) so that schematic changes can be forward-annotated. The sheet combo box in the action toolbar and the sheet thumbnails switch between sheets or add new ones; sheets can also be reordered by dragging thumbnails or with EDIT.
tools.usage: Control Panel > File > Open > Schematic, double-click a .sch, or EDIT name.sch
tools.example:
EDIT .s3;        # show sheet 3
EDIT .s5 .s2;    # move sheet 5 in front of sheet 2
tools.notes: Each sheet keeps its own zoom level; modules of a hierarchical schematic are edited with EDIT name.mod.

tools.name: Library Editor
tools.description: The editor window for part libraries (*.lbr). It opens on a table of contents listing the devices, footprints, 3D packages and symbols, from which items can be opened, renamed, duplicated or deleted; Add buttons create or import items and Import 3D Package copies a 3D package from another library, adds one from the web or creates one with the package generator. The Edit dialog (Devices/Footprints/Symbols tabs) opens an item by typing its name in the New field, and Import... copies items from in-use libraries, including every 3D package, footprint and symbol a device references.
tools.usage: File > Open > Library or OPEN name.lbr; then EDIT name.dev | name.fpt | name.sym
tools.notes: Footprints were called packages before EAGLE 9.1 (.pac is still accepted by EDIT). Use OPEN, not USE, to edit a library.

tools.name: Text Editor
tools.description: EAGLE's built-in editor for plain text such as ULPs and script files, with printing, search and replace (regular expressions) and UTF-8 storage. Instead of it you can configure an external editor in Options > User interface; its command line may contain %F (file name), %L (line) and %C (column, currently always 1), and a single '-' prevents EAGLE from ever opening a text editor.
tools.usage: File > Open/New > ULP, Script or Text; configure Options > User interface > External text editor
tools.example: External text editor: "C:\Program Files\Notepad++\notepad++.exe" -n%L "%F"
tools.notes: EAGLE cannot see whether an external editor modified a file, File > Save all does not save it, and such windows are not stored in the project; the update report of converted old files always uses the internal editor.

tools.name: Editor panels
tools.description: Dockable panels that show settings and data without nested properties dialogs: Inspector, Selection Filter, Design Manager and Sheets. Closed panels are reopened from the editor's View menu and come back where they were last shown; they can float, dock at any window border or be stacked as tabs.
tools.usage: Editor > View > <panel>, or SET INSPECTOR | SELECTION_FILTER | DESIGN_MANAGER | SHEETS OFF | ON | TOGGLE;

tools.name: Inspector
tools.description: Shows and edits the properties of the current selection in schematic, board, symbol and footprint editors. For one object all properties are listed; for several, only the common ones, filterable with the 'Show Types' checkboxes, and edits apply immediately to all selected objects. It also offers Quick Actions (rotate, mirror, replace, delete, ripup, align ...), a Selected Objects table and direct editing, adding or deleting of attributes (an added attribute is created on all selected objects, keeping existing values).
tools.usage: Select objects with GROUP (or with Group default on), then edit in the Inspector; SET INSPECTOR OFF | ON | TOGGLE;
tools.example: GROUP all 0603 capacitors, then in the Inspector change 'Value' to 100nF and add attribute MPN = GRM188R71C104KA01 for all of them.

tools.name: Selection Filter
tools.description: Restricts which objects commands can pick, without changing visibility. The Type Filter limits selection to chosen object types (for example only wires and vias) and the Layer Filter limits it to chosen layers or presets; a Reset button restores the defaults. Both filters can also be set from scripts.
tools.usage: SET SELECTTYPES types; SET SELECTLAYERS layers; SET SELECTION_FILTER OFF | ON | TOGGLE;

tools.name: Sheets panel
tools.description: Lists the sheets of the current schematic. Its context menu adds and removes sheets and edits their descriptions.
tools.usage: Schematic editor > View > Sheets; SET SHEETS OFF | ON | TOGGLE;
tools.example: Right-click in the Sheets panel > Add sheet, then Edit description 'Power supply'.

tools.name: Design Manager
tools.description: A dockable portal panel available in schematic and board with two tabs: Browser (views of parts, nets, devices, signals and groups) and Filters (dynamic rule-based selections). The Filters tab works the same in both editors but with editor-specific criteria, and schematic and board filters are saved separately.
tools.usage: Editor > View > Design Manager; SET DESIGN_MANAGER OFF | ON | TOGGLE;
tools.example: SET DESIGN_MANAGER ON;   # then pick Browser > Nets to inspect the pin connections of net SDA

tools.name: Design Manager Browser tab
tools.description: Hierarchical views selected from a dropdown: in the schematic Parts (parts per sheet and their items) and Nets (sheet > net > segments > pin connections), in the board Devices (top and bottom) and Signals (net class > signal > pads/SMDs/wires). The Groups view in both editors shows persistent groups (with Main and module scopes and an [Ungrouped] row) plus an Items section, and its menus provide New Group, Add To, Remove From, Ungroup, Clear Group, Delete and Properties.
tools.usage: Design Manager > Browser > view dropdown (Parts | Nets | Devices | Signals | Groups); double-click a row for its properties
tools.example: Browser > Groups > select 'USB' > More > Clear Group   (empties the group but keeps its members in the design)
tools.notes: Group annotations are controlled with SET GROUP_ANNOTATIONS OFF | ON | HOVERONLY; see also NEWGROUP, EDITGROUP and UNGROUP.

tools.name: Design Manager Filters tab
tools.description: Builds dynamic selections from filter criteria joined by AND/OR into a boolean expression, either with the Filter Composer or by typing the expression; the two stay synchronised and an invalid expression is flagged. Every criterion must be enclosed in parentheses and has one of three forms: binary (Type operator Target), unary (Type Target, optionally negated with !) or keyword (Type, optionally negated). Filters can be saved in the design or in the EAGLE settings and reloaded from the dropdown, which also runs them.
tools.usage: Design Manager > Filters > compose criteria or type an expression > run / save

parameters.name: Operators
parameters.description: =, !=, <, >, <=, >= (not every criterion supports all).

parameters.name: Name / Value targets
parameters.description: '*' wildcards allowed; Value accepts engineering notation (1pF, 10uH, 1Meg) and is compared numerically unless quoted as '47k'.

parameters.name: Numeric targets
parameters.description: Length, Width, PositionX/Y, Rotation with units cm, mm, mil or mic.

tools.example:
((ObjectType = Part) AND (Name = R*) AND (HasFootprint *0603*))
((ObjectType = Part) AND !(HasSpiceModel R))
tools.notes: Schematic filters are saved in the schematic, board filters in the board; names may repeat between design and global scope.

tools.name: Filter criteria types
tools.description: The criteria available in Design Manager filter expressions and the editors they apply to. Binary: ObjectType, Value, Name, Width, Length, PositionX, PositionY, Rotation (SCH and BRD), DeviceName (SCH), PadCount, ViaShape, PadShape (BRD). Unary: InNetClass, InFilter (reuse another filter), InLibrary, IsMemberOfBus, InModule, HasAttribute, HasSpiceModel, HasFootprint, HasPin, HasPad (SCH and BRD), InNet and OnSheet (SCH), OnLayer and OnSignal (BRD). Keyword: IsLocked (BRD), IsMirrored, IsSimReady, RequiresSpiceModel, Has3DModel (SCH and BRD).
tools.usage: (Criterion Operator Target) | (Criterion Target) | !(Criterion Target) | (Keyword) | !(Keyword)
tools.example:
((ObjectType = Part) AND (InLibrary rcl))
((OnSignal GND) AND (OnLayer 16))
((ObjectType = Part) AND !(Has3DModel))

tools.name: Forward & Back Annotation
tools.description: The automatic link that keeps a schematic and its board consistent while both are loaded: adding a part in the schematic places its footprint at the board's lower left (with Pwr pins connected to their supply signals), deleting a part removes the footprint (connected wires stay), deleting an element in the board removes all its gates from every sheet, and PINSWAP/GATESWAP rewire the board. Board and schematic belong together only if they have the same file name (.brd/.sch) in the same directory, and both must be open during editing.
tools.usage: Automatic; keep both files loaded (opening one opens the other)
tools.example: Open demo2.sch (demo2.brd opens too) > ADD a capacitor on sheet 1 > its footprint appears next to the board outline, connected by airwires.
tools.notes: After adding or removing pads of signals with polygons, or UNDO/REDO of such steps, run RATSNEST to recalculate polygon thermals. Moving apart two parts whose pins touched creates a net wire to keep the board unchanged; REPLACE checks that all pin-assigned pads exist in the new footprint.

tools.name: Consistency Check
tools.description: Forward & back annotation requires the board and schematic to contain equivalent parts/elements and nets/signals. When a pair is loaded EAGLE checks consistency markers and, if they disagree, offers an ERC, which cross-checks both files: if they match, annotation is activated, otherwise the ERC list shows the consistency errors and annotation stays off until you fix them (NAME, VALUE, PINSWAP, REPLACE, ATTRIBUTE, CHANGE PACKAGE ...) and run ERC again.
tools.usage: ERC (with the board loaded) > fix the listed consistency errors > ERC again
tools.example: Warning 'No Forward&Back Annotation will be performed!' after editing the board alone > open both files > ERC > rename C7 to C17 in the board as listed > ERC > 'Board and schematic are consistent'.
tools.notes: Tolerated differences: board elements without pads/SMDs, extra elements whose pads are unconnected, and signals without a net counterpart as long as they touch no pad/SMD. Consistency errors cannot be approved.

tools.name: Back Annotation limitations
tools.description: While the schematic is loaded, some board operations cannot be back-annotated and are refused with a message: adding or copying elements with pads or SMDs, deleting an airwire, defining connections with SIGNAL, and pasting board data that contains elements with pads/SMDs or signals with connections. Do these operations in the schematic so they are forward-annotated.
tools.usage: Perform connectivity changes in the Schematic Editor
tools.example: Instead of SIGNAL GND R1 2 C1 1; in the board, draw NET GND between R1 pin 2 and C1 pin 1 in the schematic.
tools.notes: Closing the schematic window lifts the restriction but risks losing consistency.

tools.name: Command syntax
tools.description: Editor commands can be typed, chosen from menus or icons, bound to keys with ASSIGN or read from script files, and all of these can be mixed. Upper-case words in the syntax are keywords (case does not matter when typing and they may be abbreviated as long as they stay unambiguous), lower-case words are values, '|' separates alternatives, '..' means repetition and a bullet marks a mouse click. Sizes and coordinates may carry units (mm, mic, mil, in); without a unit the current GRID unit applies, and a semicolon ends a command that has fewer than its maximum number of parameters.
tools.usage: COMMAND [KEYWORD] value..;
tools.notes: In scripts and in commands returned by a ULP with exit() always use '.' as decimal separator, even if your locale allows ','.

tools.name: Coordinates in commands
tools.description: Mouse clicks can be given as text coordinates (x y) in the current grid unit or with explicit units per axis, which is mainly used in scripts. (@) refers to the current mouse position, and modifier letters after the opening parenthesis simulate keys and buttons or change the coordinate type: > right button, A Alt, C Ctrl, S Shift, R relative to the mark, P polar relative to the mark (radius, angle in degrees counterclockwise).
tools.usage: (x y) | (100mil 2mm) | (@) | (modifiers x y), modifiers from > A C S R P in any order
tools.notes: Without a mark, R and P coordinates are relative to the drawing origin; polar input is stored as ordinary x/y values.

tools.name: eagle command line
tools.description: EAGLE can be started with options, a file name and (for boards) a layer list. Options taking a value have the value appended with or without a space (-Wmywheel.whl or -W mywheel.whl); flag options are switched with '+'/'-' and can be combined behind one dash. A file without extension defaults to .brd, and a file named eagle.epf is opened as a project.
tools.usage: eagle [ options [ filename [ layer ] ] ]

parameters.name: Flag notation
parameters.description: -e or -e+ switches on, -e- switches off; '-' in the option list means off by default, '+' on by default.

parameters.name: Combined flags
parameters.description: -ecf = aperture emulation on, positive coordinates on, fill pads on; -ec-f+ = emulation on, positive coordinates off, fill pads on.

parameters.name: Tolerances
parameters.description: -D (draw), -E (drill), -F (flash) with 0.1 = 10 %; a value without sign applies to both directions, e.g. -D+0.1 -D-0.05.

tools.example:
eagle D:\Work\PowerSupply\eagle.epf
eagle -U- D:\Work\demo2.brd
eaglecon -X -dGERBER_RS274X -oD:\out\demo2.cmp D:\Work\demo2.brd 1 17 18
tools.notes: Paths containing spaces must be quoted; all options go on one line.

tools.name: eagle -C
tools.description: Loads the given board, schematic or library and executes one or more semicolon-separated editor commands as if typed into its command line. The file must be named (it need not exist); eagle.scr is not run, -S is ignored, user settings are not written back to eaglerc and the last open project is not reopened. The special form -C "" (with a space before the quotes) just starts EAGLE without eagle.scr and without loading a project.
tools.usage: eagle -C "command; command;" file.brd|file.sch|file.lbr
tools.example:
eagle -C "window (1 1) (2 2);" myboard.brd
eagle -C "RUN bom.ulp; QUIT" D:\Work\demo2.sch
tools.notes: Needs the interactive editor, therefore a working Autodesk sign-in since the June 2026 licensing shutdown; for unattended output use eaglecon -X instead.

tools.name: eagle -X
tools.description: Runs the CAM Processor from the command line instead of opening the editors. Combined with -dCAMJOB and -j it processes a complete JSON CAM job; combined with a legacy device (-dGERBER_RS274X, -dEXCELLON, -dPS ...) and a layer list it writes a single output file. It reads the board file directly and, as checked on 9.6.0 in September 2026, still works without an Autodesk sign-in after the licensing shutdown.
tools.usage: eaglecon -X [-N] -d<device|CAMJOB> [-j<job.cam>] -o<file|dir> [other CAM options] board.brd [layers]
tools.example: eaglecon -X -N -dCAMJOB -jexample_2_layer.cam -oD:\out board.brd
tools.notes: Use eaglecon.exe on Windows so that messages reach the console; the legacy device, tolerance and flag options are described in the CAM Processor category.

tools.name: eagle -d
tools.description: Selects the output device for the command-line CAM Processor: either one of the legacy drivers defined in eagle.def (GERBER_RS274X, EXCELLON, PS, EPS, HPGL, ...) or the keyword CAMJOB to process a whole JSON CAM job named with -j. -d? lists the available drivers.
tools.usage: -d<DEVICE> | -dCAMJOB | -d?
tools.example:
eaglecon -d?
eaglecon -X -dEXCELLON -oboard.drd board.brd 44 45

tools.name: eagle -j
tools.description: Gives the path of the JSON CAM job file to process when -dCAMJOB is used. The job defines all Gerber, drill, assembly and drawing outputs, so one call produces the complete manufacturing set.
tools.usage: -j<path\job.cam>   (only together with -X -dCAMJOB)
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB -j"C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\examples\cam\examples\example_4_layer.cam" -oD:\out D:\Work\board.brd

tools.name: eagle -o
tools.description: Names the output of the command-line CAM Processor: the output file for a single legacy device, or the output directory when a CAM job with several files is processed (-dCAMJOB -j). Since 9.5 a non-existent output folder is created automatically for CAM jobs.
tools.usage: -o<file> | -o<directory>
tools.example:
eaglecon -X -dGERBER_RS274X -oD:\out\board.stc board.brd 29
eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB -jjob.cam -oD:\out\rev_B board.brd

tools.name: eagle -A
tools.description: Selects the assembly variant for which the command-line CAM Processor generates data. Without -A the variant the board was saved with (the default variant) is used, which matters for BOM, pick-and-place and paste-mask outputs where unpopulated parts are left out.
tools.usage: -A<variant name>
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB -jexample_2_layer.cam -AlowCost -oD:\out\lowCost board.brd

tools.name: eagle -N
tools.description: Suppresses command-line prompts, warnings and informational messages so that CAM jobs run without interruption in batch files. Since 9.2 it suppresses all output messages completely.
tools.usage: -N   (-N- to allow messages)
tools.example: eaglecon -X -N -dCAMJOB -jexample_2_layer.cam -oD:\out board.brd

tools.name: eagle -U
tools.description: Uses a specific user settings file instead of the version-specific default eaglerc (on Windows C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Eagle\settings\<X.Y.Z>\eaglerc, on macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Eagle/settings/<X.Y.Z>/eaglerc, on Linux ~/.local/share/Eagle/settings/<X.Y.Z>/eaglerc). -U- reads and writes no eaglerc at all, which is useful for reproducible automated runs.
tools.usage: -U<full path of settings file> | -U-
tools.example:
eagle -UC:/Settings/eaglerc5.usr
eaglecon -X -U- -dCAMJOB -jjob.cam -oout board.brd
tools.notes: On the first start of a new version EAGLE offers to import settings from the previous version's eaglerc.

tools.name: eagle -S
tools.description: Names the script that the editor runs when a window opens, instead of the default eagle.scr. It is ignored when -C is used and the CAM Processor never reads the script.
tools.usage: -S<script file>
tools.example: eagle -SD:\Company\scripts\company.scr D:\Work\demo2.sch

tools.name: eaglecon.exe
tools.description: The Windows console version of EAGLE (the help places it in the 'bin' folder; in the 9.6.0 installation it sits next to eagle.exe in the program folder). It is identical to eagle.exe but keeps its connection to the console, so it is the program to call from batch files and automation for command-line CAM processing; eaglecon -? prints the version banner and the option list.
tools.usage: eaglecon [options] [file [layers]]
tools.example: "C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\eaglecon.exe" -X -N -dCAMJOB -jexample_2_layer.cam -oD:\out D:\Work\board.brd
tools.notes: If an EAGLE window was opened from the console, close EAGLE before closing the console; closing the console first shuts EAGLE down uncontrolled and loses unsaved changes.
